more_info.banned_in:
Approved in the EU.
Approved in the US.
US food use is subject to the listed CFR provisions and their conditions, checked in 2026.
No current country-wide food-use ban was confirmed in the regulatory sources checked in 2026.
The permissions checked in 2026 apply only to the specified preparations, food uses and conditions.
more_info.overview: Sodium benzoate is a sodium salt of benzoic acid, specified as a distinct chemical preparation for food manufacture. Its preservative role is to limit spoilage caused by microorganisms and extend the storage life of the food. The specified material is supplied as white powder or crystalline material. The specification identifies water solubility as one of its properties.
more_info.daily_intake:
0–20 mg/kg body weight/day, combined JECFA benzoate group expressed as benzoic acid equivalents (JECFA, 2021).
5 mg/kg body weight/day, combined benzoic acid and benzoates expressed as benzoic acid (EFSA, 2016).
more_info.side_effects:
Food-use exposure estimates exceeded the group limit in some children.
The reviewed evidence did not indicate genotoxic or cancer effects.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain other confectionery including breath freshening microsweets; chewing gum; fruit juices as defined by Directive 2001/112/EC and vegetable juices; flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products; sauces; extra jam and extra jelly as defined by Directive 2001/113/EC.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
